title: Composite and Row Types knowledge check

questions.prompt: When is a PostgreSQL specialized type a good fit?
options: When its type-specific operations express the domain clearly and the team understands its constraints.
Whenever every relational table can be replaced by one array.
Only when no constraints or indexes are needed.
Whenever data validation should be removed.
questions.answer_key: When its type-specific operations express the domain clearly and the team understands its constraints.
questions.explanation: Specialized types can simplify particular domains, but type choice should fit query needs, constraints and maintainability.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports a correct implementation of composite and row types?
options: Concatenate user input into SQL and remove permission checks
Assume one successful example proves security and recovery
Apply the largest possible change before collecting a baseline
Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
questions.answer_key: Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
questions.explanation: A controlled example makes the prerequisites and expected behavior explicit. Verification of an edge case helps show whether the idea behind composite and row types is understood.

questions.prompt: When an example related to composite and row types produces an unexpected result, what is the strongest next step?
options: Grant administrator privileges to every application role
Ignore the returned result and assume the write succeeded
Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
Disable constraints and retry until the command succeeds
questions.answer_key: Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
questions.explanation: Database troubleshooting should be evidence-led and performed with suitable permissions. Broad privileges or disabling integrity checks may hide the cause and create new failures.
